channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) has published a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach for rehabilitating athletes with hamstring strain injury, providing evidence-based guidance for physical therapists.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of iTBS and rTMS Combined with Robotic Rehabilitation on Ambulation and Lower Extremity Motor Function in Chronic SCI Patients.
item.description: This single-center, single-blind RCT (n=30) found that both rTMS and iTBS combined with robotic rehabilitation improved lower-extremity motor function, SCIM III scores, and 10 MWT in chronic SCI patients, with median LEMS improvements of 4.0 and 5.0, respectively, versus 0.0 for sham, at 4-week follow-up.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of six studies (n=173 ACLR, n=79 controls) found that shear wave elastography (SWE) consistently detected reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus (Hedges' g -1.10 to -1.21) and semitendinosus stiffness (g -1.29 to -1.64 after hamstring harvest) in operative limbs after ACLR, linking these deficits to quadriceps strength, knee function, and landing biomechanics.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, comprising structured on-field rehabilitation, return to team training, return to competitive match play, and sustained performance, underpinned by four interdependent pillars.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Somatosensory Interventions on Sensory, Motor, and Balance Functions in Individuals with Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 9 RCTs (330 participants) found that somatosensory interventions significantly improved Berg Balance Scale scores in stroke patients compared to conventional therapy, but no significant pooled effects were observed for upper limb motor function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with meta-analysis (13 trials) found that very low-certainty evidence shows percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) added to therapeutic exercise (TE) is not superior to sham plus TE or TE alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence suggests PNE plus TE may offer greater short- and medium-term pain reduction compared with dry needling (DN) plus TE in tendinopathies, but not in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low-to-moderate exercise doses were associated with short-term clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for chronic low back pain, with limited additional benefit at higher exposure. Optimal doses were predicted as 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence on whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain intensity, disability, and global recovery in people with specific or nonspecific spinal pain, with most studies reporting no clear association and high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that both mirror therapy (MD -2.60, 95% CI -5.83 to -0.63, p=0.004) and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (MD -3.00, 95% CI -6.23 to -0.23, p=0.008) improved lower extremity motor function more than conventional rehabilitation in subacute stroke patients, with no significant difference between the two adjunct therapies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: This review provides an anatomy-based approach to calf injuries, emphasizing refined anatomical characterization for diagnosis, management, and return-to-sport decisions, while highlighting limitations in evidence linking specific patterns to prognosis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Identifying heterogeneous patterns of real-world upper limb use beyond motor severity: a cross-sectional sensor-based study in people with subacute stroke
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 101 subacute stroke patients used accelerometers and FMA-UL to identify six heterogeneous upper limb activity patterns, distinguishing between motor deficits, learned non-use, and UL inattention. Clinical variables like ARAT, MAL, and UL inattention were key differentiators.
item.author: J NeuroEng Rehabil

item.title: The effects of route previewing on adaptive gait and gaze behaviour under cognitive dual-task conditions in older adults
item.description: A study (n=39 older adults) found that route previewing before gait initiation attenuates the negative effects of cognitive load on adaptive gait, reducing stepping errors and cross-steps (p < .001) and improving gaze efficiency, likely by supporting visual motor planning.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Transitions and predictive factors of cognitive frailty states in rural older adults: a prospective cohort study
item.description: A prospective cohort study of 3,243 rural older adults from China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study found cognitive frailty (CF) to be reversible, with the intensity of recovery from reversible CF (RCF) to only non-dementia cognitive impairment (NDCI) being 0.429 (95% CI 0.359–0.512), highlighting early RCF as a key intervention window.
item.author: BMC Geriatrics

item.title: The Role of Psychosocial Factors in Returning to Physical Activity and Sport Among Female Football Players After Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury: A Scoping Review
item.description: A scoping review identified psychosocial factors influencing return to physical activity and sport among female football players after ACL injury. Uncertainty, fear, lack of confidence, and poor social support were perceived barriers, while confidence, motivation, strong social support, and athletic identity were facilitators.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: Experiences of sexual rehabilitation post-stroke among LGBTQI+ stroke survivors and their partners: a qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative phenomenological study explored the experiences of 18 LGBTQI+ stroke survivors and 5 partners regarding post-stroke sexual rehabilitation. Key themes included sexuality being addressed post-stroke, negative interactions with health professionals, and sexuality being absent in rehabilitation.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Barriers and facilitators of decision-making in home-based rehabilitation exercise among older adults following total knee arthroplasty: A qualitative study.
item.description: A qualitative study of 21 older adults post-total knee arthroplasty in China identified three themes and 10 subthemes regarding decision-making for home-based rehabilitation exercises, highlighting impulsive avoidance responses (e.g., pain, fear) as barriers and rational adherence (e.g., perceived threat of poor prognosis, goal-directed willpower) as facilitators.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Burden of fall-related injury and its predictors among stroke survivors attending comprehensive specialized hospitals in the Amhara Regional State, Ethiopia, 2024: A multicenter prospective study.
item.description: A multicenter cross-sectional study in Ethiopia (N=269) found the prevalence of fall-related injury among stroke survivors to be 79.9% (95% CI: 75.1-84.4). Age >65, rural residence, and injuries during walking and turning were significant predictors.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Recent highlights in pulmonary rehabilitation research.
item.description: This narrative review summarizes pulmonary rehabilitation research between January 2021 and May 2026, highlighting expanded scope beyond stable COPD to various chronic respiratory diseases, alternative PR models, and economic benefits, while noting ongoing challenges in access and long-term maintenance.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Short term effectiveness of dry needling and instrument assisted soft tissue mobilization in knee osteoarthritis patients - a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (N=34) comparing dry needling (DN), Instrument Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization (IASTM), and conventional treatment (CT) for knee osteoarthritis found DN superior in reducing pain and improving function and ROM at 4 and 6 weeks, followed by IASTM and CT.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Adherence to home-based exercise therapy in adults with non-specific chronic low back pain: a cross-sectional study of 491 participants of the ComPaRE cLBP e-cohort (ADHERE II).
item.description: A cross-sectional study of 491 adults with non-specific chronic low back pain found that 45% were adherent to home-based exercise therapy. Higher levels of physical activity before cLBP onset, lower intensity of cLBP, and lower burden of treatment were associated with higher adherence, while supervision showed no significant influence.
item.author: PubMed
